title.zh: 一顆星，揭開銀河系中心黑洞的「自轉之謎」
title.en: One Star, One Shot: Measuring the Spin of the Milky Way's Black Hole

summary.zh:
【總結】天文學家在銀河系中心發現了一顆代號 S301 的暗弱恆星，它正以 8.7 年的超短週期緊密繞行超大質量黑洞人馬座 A*（Sgr A*），其近心點距離僅約黑洞史瓦西半徑的 136 至 142 倍。這項發現由 GRAVITY+ 團隊利用歐洲南方天文台的甚大望遠鏡（VLT）干涉儀完成，是迄今唯一能在未來十年內直接測量 Sgr A* 自轉速度的恆星軌道實驗。

【研究問題】黑洞的自轉是愛因斯坦廣義相對論中極核心的未解之謎。儘管我們已精確測得 Sgr A* 的質量（約 430 萬倍太陽質量），但其自轉參數至今仍是盲點——因為黑洞自轉對時空的扭曲效應隨距離以 r⁻³ 衰減，極其微弱。過去最接近 Sgr A* 的恆星 S2 雖然已觀測到史瓦西進動，但其近心點距離過大，自轉效應（倫茲-提爾林進動）太小，需要漫長的數據累積才能探測。

【研究方法】研究團隊自 2017 年起，每月使用 GRAVITY 干涉儀對銀河系中心進行近紅外波段觀測，累積超過 80–100 小時/年的觀測時間。他們運用自研的影像重建演算法 GRAVITY-RESOLVE（GR），在複雜的恆星場中識別出微弱的新天體。透過 19 個時段的.astrometric 定位數據，結合馬可夫鏈蒙特卡洛方法擬合軌道，並納入羅默延遲與史瓦西相對論修正，精確勾勒出 S301 的軌道參數。

【結果】S301 的軌道參數極為極端：半長軸僅 83 毫角秒（比 S2 小 33%），偏心率高达 0.983，近心點距離約 136–142 個史瓦西半徑，在近心點時速度高達 25,600 公里/秒（約 8.5% 光速）。其史瓦西進動每圈達 1.9°，而倫茲-提爾林進動（自轉訊號）每圈約 0.11°——這個訊號在未來十年內有望被 GRAVITY+ 與極大望遠鏡（ELT/MICADO）的光譜觀測所捕捉。研究團隊模擬顯示，若持續觀測至 2035 年，自轉參數的不確定度可低於 0.2，達到超過 5σ 的偵測顯著性。S301 的極高偏心率暗示它可能源自希爾斯機制（Hills mechanism）——一對緊密雙星被 Sgr A* 的潮汐力撕裂後，其中一顆被俘虜至此軌道，另一顆則被彈射為超高速星。
summary.en:
**Summary:** Astronomers have discovered S301, a faint main-sequence star orbiting the supermassive black hole at the center of our galaxy, Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), on the tightest and most relativistic orbit ever recorded. With an 8.7-year period and a pericentre distance of just 136–142 Schwarzschild radii, S301 is the first stellar object sensitive enough to the black hole's spin to allow a direct measurement within the next decade. The discovery was made by the GRAVITY+ collaboration using the Very Large Telescope interferometer.

**Problem:** The spin of a black hole is one of the last fundamental properties of Sgr A* that remains unmeasured. While the black hole's mass has been pinned down to sub-percent precision, its rotation rate is hidden because the frame-dragging effects of a spinning Kerr metric decay as r⁻³ — making them extraordinarily difficult to detect. Previous candidates like the famous S2 star have probed the Schwarzschild precession (a 1PN effect), but their pericentre distances are too large for the much weaker Lense–Thirring (spin) precession to be observable on any practical timescale.

**Approach:** Starting in 2017, the team conducted monthly near-infrared interferometric observations of the central arcsecond around Sgr A* using GRAVITY on the VLT, accumulating roughly 80–100 hours per year. S301 was first spotted in spring 2023 as a faint source moving rapidly near Sgr A*. The team then conducted dedicated follow-up campaigns in 2024 and 2025, eventually recovering pre-discovery detections in 2017 and 2021 data. They used a custom image-reconstruction code called GRAVITY-RESOLVE (GR), which combines Bayesian inference with a forward model of the instrument, to locate the star at micro-arcsecond precision. Orbital fitting was performed with a χ² minimization that includes Römer delay and first post-Newtonian (1PN) Schwarzschild corrections, using Markov chain sampling to explore the parameter space.

**Results:** S301 holds several records: its semi-major axis is 83 milliarcseconds (33% smaller than S2's), its eccentricity is an extreme 0.983, and its pericentre distance is roughly ten times closer than S2's. At pericentre, the star reaches 25,600 km/s — 8.5% the speed of light. The Schwarzschild precession amounts to 1.9° per orbit, while the Lense–Thirring spin contribution is about 0.11° per revolution — a signal comparable to the precession GRAVITY already measured for S2. Mock-data simulations show that with continued observations through 2035, the dimensionless spin parameter χ could be constrained to an uncertainty of less than 0.2, yielding a >5σ detection. The star's extreme eccentricity points to a Hills mechanism origin: a compact binary was torn apart by Sgr A*'s tidal forces, with S301 captured onto this relativistic orbit and its companion ejected as a hyper-velocity star.

keyArticle.title: Discovery of a star sensitive to the spin of Sagittarius A*
